title: Founding curls to the ground now
question: Do the founded bodies lie flat on the soil, at rest and separate -- or do any overlap or stand off the surface?
context_md: Founding used to demand a straight n-cell run at one height; it now walks the spine along the ground contour (flat-with-foothold, then a step up or down, then flat unconditionally as a last resort) so a long body can curl to fit where a two-cell body already stood fine. This crop is the played bed's nest band at frame 6,100, right after the colony's timeline event founds it -- a still is honest here because founding is a placement, not motion.
